title: Regional affinity harness and staged evacuation for dedicated lane exhaustion
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: when a tenant's requests exhaust their Dedicated capacity in a region, upstream routing currently performs an immediate spill to hosted variants which causes sudden latency/cost spikes and occasional model-quality regressions. Goal: implement a region-affinity harness that attempts graceful staged evacuation of traffic from Dedicated -> nearby Dedicated (if available) -> percent-based hosted shepherding with progressive backoff and quality-preserving model variant mapping. Deliverables: routing policy library changes, circuit controller, canary rules for percent-based host spill, rollout playbook, dashboard metrics and alerts, and an automated rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Tenant requests are routed off exhausted Dedicated lanes using a staged policy: local rebind -> soft-lease to another Dedicated region -> progressive hosted shepherding with pre-mapped compatible model variant. 2) Token-cost and p99 latency for routed tenants increases by no more than 20% compared to baseline during evacuation. 3) System provides clear audit events for every policy decision and exposes per-tenant debug traces in Console. 4) Automatic demotion stops if quality regression metrics (BLEU/ROUGE surrogate or eval harness) cross threshold. 5) All changes covered by unit/integration tests and integration smoke runbook.
notes: This ticket builds on capacity steering experiments from last quarter. We will reuse model-compatibility table (model_variant_map) but extend it with compatibility scores and quality deltas observed in synthetic evals. We'll also add an emergency bypass that pins traffic to the original Dedicated model in read-only degraded mode for short windows.
technical_decisions: Prefer progressive percent-based spill rather than binary failover to reduce client-visible latency jumps
Use a soft-lease mechanism (ephemeral routing reservation) to attempt cross-region Dedicated rebinding before touching hosted
Map model variants using a compatibility score and apply heuristic demotion with grace windows
implementation_plan: 1) Add routing policy DSL: region_affinity + staged_evacuation steps
2) Implement soft-lease controller with TTL and optimistic handoff
3) Integrate percent-shepherding engine into the orchestrator with throttles per-tenant
4) Wire audit events and Console debug traces
5) Run interop tests with Dedicated autoscaler and the host fallback policy simulator
6) Roll out as opt-in feature flag for a small set of canary tenants
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: sudden quality regressions when routed to hosted variants. Mitigation: precompute variant compatibility scores and gate percent-shepherding by eval thresholds.
Risk: cascading capacity movement between regions causing oscillation. Mitigation: add cooldowns and hysteresis on soft-lease reclamation.
Risk: billing surprises for customers. Mitigation: expose per-tenant predicted cost delta in Console and optional pre-approval webhook.
tests: Unit: routing DSL parser + policy executor
Integration: orchestrator + soft-lease end-to-end with Dedicated emulator
Load: simulated tenant exhaustion runs and p99 latency measurements
Quality: synthetic prompt set eval comparing original Dedicated model vs hosted variants
observability: New metrics: evacuations_started, evacuations_step_counts, percent_shepherded, compatibility_score_histogram
Dashboard: per-tenant evacuation timeline and cost delta preview
runbook: Steps to troubleshoot: 1) Look up routing.decision events in Console, 2) If quality regressions > threshold, flip feature-flag to pause shepherding for tenant, 3) If latency spike > SLA, trigger emergency pin to previous Dedicated model lane and notify SRE on-call. Postmortem template linked in attachments.
